## The claim

Read-backed phasing resolves, or explicitly fails to resolve, the configuration of the top candidate pair.

**Prediction if true.** For the top candidate pair WhatsHap and HapCUT2 either agree on a phase chain closed through the intervening heterozygous SNVs, or report the exact gap that breaks it, with the fraction of the distance covered.

**What would refute it.** Neither outcome is produced — a tooling failure, re-run before any phase conclusion is drawn.

| 2 | supported | 0.70 | Supported in the sense the claim was written: the phaser either closes a chain or names the gap, and it named the gap. WhatsHap resolved 6,823 blocks genome-wide and placed neither of the lead gene's two alleles in any of them. The cause is measured — 10,911 bp apart, four heterozygous variants between them at ~2.7 kb mean spacing against a ~266 bp sequencing fragment, so no fragment bridges consecutive links and the chain cannot start; depth there is 43.7x, so this is the child's heterozygosity in this gene and not a coverage failure. What must not be lost when this is quoted: the useful outcome did NOT happen. Step 2 cannot demonstrate that the two alleles sit on different copies, so the trans configuration rests on step 4's population estimate, which its own plan calls poorly calibrated for ultra-rare pairs. That is a limitation this step hands forward, not a result it delivers. |
